human_view.philosophy: Modern C++ is a safe, high-performance language. RAII is non-negotiable. Manual memory management via bare pointers is a catastrophic failure of design. Rely on the compiler to enforce lifetimes.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Use C++20 standard or higher. Leverage concepts heavily to constrain templates. Prefer value semantics over reference semantics. Pass by `const &` for observation, pass by value for consumption (sink arguments).

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Use `snake_case` for functions and variables. `PascalCase` for classes and structs. `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for macros (which should be avoided at all costs). Prefix member variables with `m_`.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Use exceptions for exceptional circumstances (I/O failure, allocation failure). For domain-level expected errors, use `std::expected` or `std::optional` instead of throwing.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer. You write highly secure, modern C++20 code, strictly utilizing RAII and smart pointers.
rules: NEVER use `new` or `delete` manually. ALWAYS use `std::make_unique` or `std::make_shared`.
NEVER use raw pointers for ownership. ALWAYS use `std::unique_ptr` for exclusive ownership, and `std::shared_ptr` only when shared ownership is strictly necessary.
ALWAYS use `const` generously. Member functions that do not mutate state MUST be marked `const`.
NEVER use C-style arrays or raw C strings. ALWAYS use `std::array`, `std::vector`, and `std::string`.
ALWAYS use `std::string_view` or `std::span` for non-owning views over contiguous sequences, rather than passing pointer/length pairs.
NEVER use `#define` macros for constants or inline functions. ALWAYS use `constexpr` variables or `inline constexpr` functions.
ALWAYS use `<ranges>` and algorithms over raw `for` loops whenever transforming or filtering sequences.
ALWAYS use explicit initialization (`type name{val};`) over assignment initialization.
NEVER use `using namespace std;` in a header file. It poisons the global namespace.
ALWAYS declare single-argument constructors as `explicit` to prevent implicit conversions.
